title: Telegram operator channel
description: Autonomous ticks runs can reach the operator who launched them over a messaging channel: mid-run questions, approval gates, and completion reports are delivered to the operator's personal Telegram bot and resolved back into tick state with human provenance. No cloud infrastructure — tk long-polls the Bot API directly over a channel-neutral interface (Slack et al. can slot in later) — and planning stays in-session; the channel exists for runs where the human isn't. Per-operator bots (no global bot, no webhook); secrets live in global ~/.tick/, never in the repo; workers never touch the channel — only the orchestrator; the tick is always the source of truth over the chat transcript.
acceptance_criteria:
[A10] tk channel setup telegram pairs the operator's personal bot end-to-end: token prompt → getMe verification → /start <code> pairing → secrets (token, user_id, chat_id) written to global ~/.tick/operator.json, with an optional non-secret entry offered for tracked .tick/operators.json.
[A11] No bot token ever lands under .tick/ — a test asserts tracked config contains no token-shaped string after setup.
[A12] tk tell "<message>" delivers to the paired operator's chat; with no pairing configured it exits with a distinct unconfigured code and changes nothing, so prompts can call it unconditionally.
[A13] tk ask supports all four interaction shapes with JSON in/out: free text (ForceReply), single-select buttons, multi-select toggle keyboard with Done, and an Other… free-text fallback on option questions.
[A14] Updates from any Telegram sender other than the bound user_id are ignored, and a reply/press is matched to its pending question by message id — concurrent pending questions resolve unambiguously.
[A15] An answer resolves into tick state, not just stdout: the Q&A lands as a tk note --from human with telegram identity recorded, awaiting state clears, and approve/reject button presses clear gates via a human-stamped activity entry that passes the epic close-out gate audit.
[A16] The tick is the source of truth: after resolution (by answer or out-of-band tk approve), the Telegram message is edited to show the outcome and its buttons removed; a stale press gets an already-resolved acknowledgment and mutates nothing.
[A17] tk ask blocks until answered or --timeout (leaving the tick awaiting, distinct exit code); --async registers the pending question and returns immediately, with a collect command to gather answers later; multiple concurrent asks on one machine share a single getUpdates consumer (no 409s).
[A18] tk ask/tk tell and all tick-state resolution run against a channel interface; the Telegram implementation is the only place Telegram API types appear, and the test suite exercises ask/tell semantics through a fake in-memory channel.
[A19] (human judgment) The ticks skill ships an operator-channel routing section in agent-runner.md wired into the blocked-agent steps, await-handling table, completion report, and gate-clearing rules — planning stays interactive, the retro still audits every mid-run interrupt, workers never touch the channel, and prompts say operator channel, not Telegram.
[A20] (human judgment) Live end-to-end: a real run with a --requires approval tick reaches the operator's actual phone, and one button tap closes the tick.
